evidence_level: Full arXiv HTML reviewed; Springer chapter record identified
scope_and_methods: Introduces perturbation-driven causal reasoning (PdCR), using average treatment effects over image-patch interventions to attribute effects on a target segmentation region; compares against SEG-GRAD and MiSuRe on HAM10000 skin-lesion and FIVES retinal-vessel segmentation.
observed_findings: The authors report higher attribution scores than the two baselines across the tested models/datasets and reveal model-dependent segmentation strategies. limitations_and_construct_boundary: Causal image-segmentation explanation method neighbor, not manipulation detection, authenticity, or forensic localization. It is recent; generalization beyond its two medical tasks and intervention construction is unestablished.

review_conclusion: Useful emerging causal-evaluation design; do not treat its medical segmentation results as proof of forensic explanation validity.
